title: Hero photos on desktop with Reduce Motion: keep them sharp, or copy the original's soft quick reload
problem:
On a 1440 px wide desktop window in Chrome with Reduce Motion on, the original page draws the 10 tilted hero photo cards in one of two ways. On a slow first load they are sharp. On a quick reload they come out slightly soft. Only the fine detail inside the photos differs, about 3 % of the screen.

The current best build (st6-rb2, the scroll-engine fix) almost always ends with the sharp photos, on a quick reload too. Card positions, sizes, tilt and everything else on the page are the same.

Your pixel rule (PR-010) asks for an exact match under Reduce Motion. st6-rb2 shows one of the original's own two pictures, so it draws nothing new. But a quick reload compared with a quick reload differs by 3 % of the screen, above the 0.5 % limit. So it is your call.
idea:
What we know (de-breakpoints, Chrome headless, 1440x900, 2026-10-04):
- Both versions load and decode the photos the same way: full size, with the same smoothing. Same bytes in Chrome's image caches (OBSERVED); full-size decode matches Chrome's source code (CONFIRMED).
- The soft picture is Chrome's first drawing of the cards. On a quick reload, the original never draws them again (OBSERVED).
- st6-rb2 happens to redraw the photos once, about 0.8 s after load, so they end sharp (OBSERVED). Which part of st6-rb2 causes that redraw was not traced.
- An invisible redraw of the original's photos made them sharp too, 2 of 2 tries (OBSERVED).
- Why Chrome's first drawing is soft is unknown: OBSERVED in our setup, cause unknown.
- With Reduce Motion off there is no difference: 2 px on one card, 0 % of the screen.
risk: Only desktop Chrome with Reduce Motion on was checked. Phone widths with Reduce Motion (430) show no difference at all. Safari was not checked: the iPhone Simulator tool cannot turn Reduce Motion on.

a.label: Original page, quick reload (Reduce Motion on, 1440 wide)

options.name: keep
options.label: Keep st6-rb2 as it is: photos end sharp
options.idea: Change nothing. The hero photos end sharp, the same picture the original shows after a slow first load or after any redraw. The work st6-rb2 saves under Reduce Motion stays saved.
options.looksSame: It shows one of the original's own pictures. st6-rb2 on a quick reload compared with the original on a slow first load: the same pixels within 4 px² and 19 of 255 shades. After one invisible redraw of both, a quick reload of each matches within 4 px² as well.
visualDiff: Quick reload against quick reload: the photo detail is crisper in st6-rb2 on 10 cards, 3.04 % of the screen (39,415 px²), largest shade 118 of 255, up to 11,983 px² on one card. Above PR-010's 0.5 % and 2,000 px² limits.
None of it is flat colour: it is photo texture and photo edges. Nothing moves, nothing is missing, nothing changes place or size.
Slow first load against slow first load: the same picture (4 px², largest shade 19).
After any redraw (shown here with an invisible one), the original is sharp as well and the two match (4 px², 0 % of the screen).
st6-rb2 was sharp in 7 of 9 quick reloads and in between in the other 2. The original was soft in 12 of 12 quick reloads and sharp in 5 of 5 slow first loads.
Reduce Motion off (1440 wide): no difference, 2 px² on one card, 0 % of the screen.
The nav's 'EN' label also differs between slow and quick loads, in both versions alike (83 px). It is a load effect, not the fix.

gain.what: Layouts during one scripted scroll (1440, Reduce Motion)
gain.how: Census, Chrome 1440x900, two original loads and one st6-rb2 load, counts only, 2026-10-03/04. A count of work, not a timing.

gain.what: Paint events in 4 s at rest (the one cost)
gain.how: Same census; style recalcs at rest 4 -> 8, layers 102 -> 129. The ~0.8 s redraw that makes the photos sharp is part of this.

options.risk: A strict reading of your rule is not met: quick reload against quick reload is a 3 % difference. Why st6-rb2 redraws the photos was not traced, so a later fix could change which picture shows (in either direction).

shots.caption: Whole screen, quick reload (the countdown digits differ in every pair: it is a clock)
One card (Pakincht), 3x zoom, quick reload: the original is soft, st6-rb2 sharp
The same card, 3x zoom, after one invisible redraw of both: both sharp, matching
Reduce Motion off, one card, 3x zoom, quick reload: no difference

options.name: match
options.label: Make st6-rb2 copy the original's soft quick reload
options.idea:
Not achievable as a dependable result today. Honest steps:
1. Trace which part of st6-rb2 redraws the photos at about 0.8 s (one more Chrome check, about 5 minutes, counts only).
2. Stop that redraw under Reduce Motion. If the redraw comes from the work-saving change itself, stopping it may mean putting some of that work back.
3. Re-check the pixels.
Even then, the soft picture comes from a Chrome first-drawing effect whose cause we don't know. It changes with load speed: slow first loads are sharp in both versions, and any redraw makes the original sharp. We would be copying a browser quirk, not a design, and it could stop matching with any Chrome update.
options.looksSame: Not known until steps 1-3 are done. The target is the original's quick-reload picture (shown as B here). The original's own two pictures differ by 3.06 % of the screen, the same size as the difference in question.
visualDiff: Target: on a quick reload, the photos would look as soft as the original's. Slow first loads would stay sharp, as they are in both versions today.

No build exists yet, so the shot compares the original with itself: A is its quick reload (soft), B its slow first load (sharp). That is the size of the change this option would put back on quick reloads.
If it works, a quick reload would match the original to the pixel only as long as Chrome keeps the same first-drawing behaviour (cause unknown, OBSERVED).

gain.how: Depends on what step 1 finds. If the redraw is a side effect of the work-saving change, some of the saving under Reduce Motion goes away.

gain.what: Quick-reload pixel match with the original (1440, Reduce Motion)
gain.how: Needs steps 1-3. The soft picture's cause is unknown, so a match cannot be promised.

options.risk: It makes the page worse on purpose (soft photos) to copy a Chrome effect we can't explain. It may cost back part of st6-rb2's saving under Reduce Motion, and the match could break with a Chrome update or a different load speed.

shots.caption: The original itself, one card, 3x zoom. A: quick reload (soft, the target). B: slow first load (sharp).

recommended.why: st6-rb2 shows the original's own sharp picture, the one any redraw gives. Copying the soft one means copying a Chrome effect we can't explain, possibly at the cost of some of the saving.
